data.one_liner: A widget that applies a Thanos Snap particle effect to its child using a custom shader
data.what_it_does: Wrap any widget with Snappable to animate it with a particle burst effect. The effect is driven by an AnimationController or any Animation<double>.
use_when: You want a visually striking exit or entrance animation for a widget
You need a reusable, customizable particle effect without writing shader code yourself
You want to animate lists or individual items with a snap effect
avoid_when: You need a lightweight animation without shader overhead
You are targeting platforms that do not support custom shaders (e.g., older web browsers)
strengths: Uses a single shader for performance
Easy to integrate via a single widget
weaknesses: Requires adding a custom shader file to pubspec
Only works on platforms that support custom shaders (Android, iOS, web, desktop)
No support for non-animated use cases
data.setup_notes: Add the shader file to pubspec.yaml under flutter.shaders and reference the path. No build_runner needed.
data.minimal_example:
```dart
Snappable(
  animation: _controller,
  child: MyWidget(),
  outerPadding: const EdgeInsets.all(40.0),
  style: SnappableStyle(
    particleLifetime: 0.6,
    fadeOutDuration: 0.3,
    particleSpeed: 1.0,
    particleSize: const SnappableParticleSize.squareFromRelativeWidth(0.01),
  ),
);
```
